answers.statement: Holding back during the startup of an opponent's attack puts the defender into a blocking animation before the move connects; it is usually not triggered from outside the attack's maximum range and projectiles have a reduced activation range. It makes it harder to walk back out of poke range at the last moment, and slow long-range attacks stop back walking during their startup.

quotes.text: '''Proximity Guard:''' holding back during the startup of an opponent's attack will cause the defending character to enter a blocking animation before the move actually connects.
in general, proximity guard will usually not be triggered from outside the attack's maximum range.

answers.notes: The conflict is limited to the wake-up reversal buffer: Game_Data (page dated 2026-10-26) says 7 frames, Defense (2026-05-30) says 10 frames; Capcom's 2026-03-17 notes add 3 frames on wake-up and the 2026-04-15 notes remove them only when a Drive Rush overlaps the wake-up, without giving absolute numbers. The 4-frame general buffer and 7-frame dash buffer are consistent across sources. Special moves have no separate buffer figure; Capcom 202405 gives a different quantity, the input recognition frames between a motion and the button (9 frames for quarter-circle and half-circle on the ground, lines 115 and 121). Other stated items: dash input timing limits of 8 frames per step (Movement line 22), screen-freeze buffering by holding the button (Game_Data lines 41-45), sweeps got more buffer time at the end of recovery (Capcom 202506 line 200).
